issue.title: macros.md still calls %proc typed launch units beta after typed_launch_units retired

task_type_fields.proposed_change: Epic sase-1jc retired `typed_launch_units` (and every other rollout flag), so typed launch units are no longer beta. In `sase/memory/macros.md`, the directive table row for `%proc:<cmd>` / `%proc::` says "Beta stand-alone process unit", and the paragraph that begins "Beta `%proc` units (`%proc("cmd")`, `%proc(...)::` code form) dispatch natively..." also calls them beta. Drop the "Beta" qualifier from both so the note describes `%proc` (and the `%if::` script-condition form) as always available. Keep every other rule in those lines (queue fields gate dispatch only, never held after dispatch; native dispatch semantics) unchanged, then republish with `sase memory init`.

issue.creation_reason: Every sase-1jc phase recorded this PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP because the epic's auto decision macro_memory=no forbade editing macros.md without human review; the land agent files it so a human can approve the wording fix.

payload.description: Proposed by every sase-1jc phase (sase-1jc.1 through sase-1jc.12 PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP notes); the epic's auto memory decision skipped this edit
